gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-hanifi-rohingy: Noto Sans Hanifi Rohingya reads friendly and current, with a gaping c that stays visible even when the text gets small. And Phudu leads with a marker-nib line that ignores direction, so the heading hits hard while the body stays out of its way.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-hatran: Noto Sans Hatran reads smooth and approachable, its e opening wide like a funnel. Phudu is the one for bold, paperclip-bent headings with no thick-thin shifts, while Noto Sans Hatran does the quiet work of carrying the sentences.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-inscriptional-: Noto Sans Inscriptional Pahlavi reads contemporary and friendly, with small counters that never feel clogged. Noto Sans Inscriptional Pahlavi sits under Phudu, whose tails and terminals are as thick as its stems, so the heavy top line gets a light, easy follow-up.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-javanese:
Noto Sans Javanese keeps its counters open to the outside.

That makes a long stretch of text feel clean and unhurried, while Phudu's even-width curves and straights stay up in the heading.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-kawi: Phudu draws every curve and straight at a constant width, like bent pipe, with generous openings at each terminal. Noto Sans Kawi, a plain sans, stays beneath it.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-linear-a:
Round, bold and a bit playful, Phudu keeps one uninterrupted line width through every letter it draws.

Noto Sans Linear A, a plain sans, gives long text a clean, gaping c.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-linear-b: Modern and level-headed, Noto Sans Linear B gives the eye a smooth, unobstructed path around each bend. And Phudu brings its pencil-line consistency and bold display attitude to the heading, so the two sit comfortably in one layout.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-manichaean:
Phudu brings bold, heavy diagonals to the heading.

Noto Sans Manichaean, a plain sans, follows with open-mouthed e crossbars, so the heading gets all the weight and the text below stays modern and clean.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-mongolian: Noto Sans Mongolian reads neutral and modern, its terminals flaring outward at each stroke end. But Phudu looks laser-cut, one stroke width throughout, so the two feel like a loud voice beside a measured one.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-noto-sans-nko:
Phudu is bold, with no hairline thinning anywhere against its thick stems.

Noto Sans NKo, a modern sans, does its best work in the text, where its c openings stay easy to see through.
